Summary: The first commandment: God alone is to be worshipped, and nothing else may rival him.
Commandment: Worship God alone; put nothing else in his place.
Application: Jesus restates this as the first and greatest commandment (Matthew 22:37-38). Idolatry today is not only statues: anything that takes God's rightful first place — wealth, status, pleasure, self — rivals him.
Purpose: God grounds it in his own deliverance of Israel: 'I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt' (Exodus 20:2). Exclusive worship answers who God has shown himself to be.
Function: First among the Ten Words, this one is the foundation stone of the moral law — the commands God spoke from Sinai, traditionally classed moral because they bind every person in every age. Its goal was exclusive worship: a people just brought out of Egypt must know who brought them out. The evil it addressed was rival gods — wealth, status, pleasure, self — stealing God's first place. It restrained that evil by drawing a hard line: God alone is worshipped, and nothing else may rival him.
